On one hand, some researchers and philosophers argue that the human brain does possess important innate knowledge — for example, the understanding that the world includes three-dimensional objects that persist even when not observed — which was learned through evolution that the potential for language may also be inborn

On the other hand, the dominant empirical tradition, following John Locke, holds that the mind is a 'tabula rasa' (blank slate) at birth that all knowledge — including mathematical truths — is acquired solely through sensory experience ; Locke argued that it makes no sense to say we know something innately if we are not aware of it that even mathematical demonstrations require reason to discover them
